when.quote: When a customer needs to file a formal dispute for a credit card transaction (such as unauthorized charges, merchant issues, or billing errors), the agent must gather comprehensive information and call the file_credit_card_transaction_dispute_4829 tool.

starts.note: customer: start only when the customer asks to dispute a credit card charge. The agent never files a dispute the customer did not ask for. It orders a replacement card only if the customer asks to have the card cancelled and replaced.
starts.quote: However, if you've already tried contacting the merchant without success, or if the charge appears to be fraudulent, please don't hesitate to reach out to us right away.

info.about: Any 2 of date of birth, email, phone number and address. These are checked against the records.
info.ask: To verify your identity, could you please give me two of the following: your date of birth, email address, phone number or home address?

info.about: The merchant and the approximate amount or date. These are used to find the transaction_id and purchase_date in the card transaction records.

info.about: When the customer names only a merchant, or says several charges are wrong: which of the listed transactions they want to dispute, and what is wrong with each one

info.about: One of unauthorized_fraudulent_charge, duplicate_charge, incorrect_amount, goods_services_not_received, goods_services_not_as_described, canceled_subscription_still_charging or refund_never_processed. Getting something different from what was paid for (for example, a different or cheaper room or item) is goods_services_not_as_described. A charge repeated a second time is duplicate_charge.
info.ask: Which of these best describes the problem: an unauthorized or fraudulent charge, a duplicate charge, an incorrect amount, goods or services not received, goods or services not as described, a cancelled subscription that is still charging, or a refund that was never processed?

info.about: Whether the customer tried to resolve the issue with the merchant first (true or false). Asked for each transaction.
info.ask: Did you try to resolve this with the merchant first?

info.about: The date the customer noticed the issue, as MM/DD/YYYY. If the customer says 'today', get the date from get_current_time.
info.ask: When did you notice the issue?

info.about: One of full_refund, partial_refund (needs partial_refund_amount) or reversal_of_charge
info.ask: Which resolution would you like: a full refund, a partial refund (and how much), or a reversal of the charge?

info.about: The dollar amount, needed only if resolution_requested is partial_refund
info.ask: How much would you like refunded?

info.about: keep_active, or cancel_and_reissue if the customer wants the card replaced
info.ask: Would you like to keep your card active, or cancel it and have a replacement issued?

info.about: The last 4 digits of the card used for the disputed transaction
info.ask: What are the last 4 digits of the card used for this charge?

info.about: The credit card account ID. It is needed for get_card_last_4_digits and get_pending_replacement_orders_5765, shows which card holds the transaction and its tier, and is used to read the account's open date.

Needed only for cancel_and_reissue with a replacement order: the confirmed shipping address (address on file or an alternate such as a work address, with suite or unit), the replacement reason (fraud_suspected, lost, stolen, damaged, expired or other) and the shipping speed (standard, or expedited with any tier fee)
info.ask: Where should we ship the replacement card, what is the reason for the replacement, and would you like standard or expedited shipping?

steps.do: Decide eligible_for_provisional_credit using the Provisional Credit Eligibility Guidelines. All criteria must hold: account open at least 60 days (get_accounts open date vs get_time); reason is unauthorized_fraudulent_charge, duplicate_charge, or goods_services_not_received with the purchase more than 30 days ago; amount at least $25.00 and no more than the card tier's maximum; no more than 2 disputes in the past 12 months (check_dispute_history); merchant contacted for non-fraud. If any criterion fails, set it to false.
steps.quote: 15. eligible_for_provisional_credit (boolean) - Agent must determine this based on the Provisional Credit Eligibility Guidelines article in this knowledge base. Pass true or false.

rules.rule: Provisional credit is true only if ALL of these hold: the account has been open at least 60 days; the reason is unauthorized_fraudulent_charge, duplicate_charge, or goods_services_not_received with the purchase more than 30 days ago; the amount is at least $25.00 and no more than the tier maximum; no more than 2 disputes in the past 12 months; and, for non-fraud disputes, the merchant was contacted first
rules.quote: ## Eligibility Criteria — Customer is ELIGIBLE for provisional credit if ALL of the following are true:

open_questions: The credit card dispute document does not say which charge to dispute when duplicates exist. The debit document says to dispute the earliest. For credit cards, the workflow disputes each charge the customer names, with the reason the customer gives (for example, the first as fraud and the repeat as duplicate_charge).

It is unclear whether disputes filed earlier in the same conversation count toward the 'not more than 2 disputes in the past 12 months' provisional credit rule for later disputes. The workflow counts the history read before filing.
No tool is documented for counting completed replacements in the last 60 days. The tier limit can be checked only from what get_pending_replacement_orders_5765 returns.
The documents do not say whether the replacement should be ordered before or after the disputes are filed. card_action 'cancel_and_reissue' is valid either way.
It is unclear whether get_credit_card_accounts_by_user returns the card's last 4 digits. If it does not, the workflow asks the customer for them or gives them get_card_last_4_digits.

steps.do: For each chosen transaction, ask what went wrong and map the answer to exactly one dispute_reason. A charge the customer did not make maps to unauthorized_fraudulent_charge. A wrong amount maps to incorrect_amount. Charges after a cancelled subscription map to canceled_subscription_still_charging. A promised refund never applied maps to refund_never_processed.
